parts.name: count_at_most_three
parts.original_hypothesis: Root: output = sigmoid(1.208 + Linear + A3Pathway), an additive composition of linear_count_down and a3_pathway under the output sigmoid. Unconnected inputs a1:2, a4:2, a4:3, a5:3, a5:4, a6:1 are zero-effect entries (their one-hot siblings carry the same information). Net: logit ~ 80 - 20*k, where k = number of attributes taking their first value; per-indicator drops a1 19.2, a2 22.5/25.4, a3 22.2 (29.5 if a1=3), a4 17.5, a5 24.3/20.1, a6 22.4. Exhaustive check over all 432 configurations: logit 82..96 (k=0), 60..79 (k=1), 37..56 (k=2), 15..32 (k=3), -5.2..7.7 (k=4, 49% positive, depending on which attributes are first-valued: the a1/a4 indicators drop the least), <-16 (k>=5). The decision equals 'k <= 3' on 94.4% of the 432 configurations (all disagreements at k=4). The model is a saturated monotone 'at most three (sometimes four) first values' detector. Train (n=345): output median 1.0, mean 0.915; accuracy 0.41, AUC 0.81. reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
